items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I like the ones I made with Roy Williams and the 'Midnight Slows.' I like just about every one of them because Milt Buckner played so damn good with that organ

ctx.x: And Ben -- this is Nat's tune, I think it's "Blues for Johnny." "Moten Swing," "Candy," "Ben's "Early Autumn," Broken Saxophone," (inaudible). "One For Johnny," I think that's

it, "One For Johnny." Now I play a clarinet solo on there I like, but, you know, most of the things, recordings, I always find there's something I should have done. But occasionally you find things. I like the ones I made with Roy Williams and the "Midnight Slows." I like just about every one of them because Milt Buckner played so damn good with that organ and man, I could hear so many things. I got to bring you -- I got to give you -- I'll bring it over next week. I got two of them I'll bring you, "Midnight…
Any last words you want to add?
